THE LINK (Concordia University student newspaper), ELEVEN ISSUES 1988-1993
Recruitment advertising, the Seaman Memorial Cup, and the naturalist named

Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted sweep of rma-concordia-publications (p_479).
Eleven issues matched; ten on "Kanawana" and one (vol. 3 no. 22) on Weredale,
which is the false-positive class recorded at f_5421. Each item checked for
multiple text files: one each.

===============================================================================
1. THE RECRUITMENT ADVERTISING RUN, 1988-1990
===============================================================================

Vol. 8 nos. 39, 40 and 41 — 22 and 29 March 1988 and the issue between them —
carry the same display three weeks running:

  "THE EXPERIENCE THAT LASTS A LIFETIME! We specialize in fun. Kamp Kanawana is
  nestled in the heart of the Laurentians, on 1200 ACRES, near St. Sauveur. FOR
  93 YEARS we have shared our excitement for discovery, personal growth and
  leadership with the youth of Montreal. Share your enthusiasm, creativity and
  leadership with others. Kamp Kanawana is a co-ed camp for children aged 7-15."

Vol. 9 nos. 34 and 36 — 9 March 1989 and the issue before it — carry the wording
the McGill Daily also ran on 20 February 1989: "a co-ed camp for children aged
7-15, is situated in the heart of the Laurentians near St. Sauveur, on 1200
acres of land and THREE PRIVATE LAKES."

Vol. 10 nos. 34 and 38 — 6 March 1990 and later — carry a third variant: "If
you're looking for an experience that will allow you to spend your summer away…"

THREE THINGS.

(a) THE TAGLINE MOVES BACK ANOTHER YEAR. "The experience that lasts a lifetime"
    was found this morning in the McGill Daily of 20 February 1989 and written
    up as predating the 1993 documentary of that name by four years. It is here
    on 22 MARCH 1988, so the margin is five years and the phrase was in use
    across at least two student papers.

(b) "FOR 93 YEARS", IN MARCH 1988, IS THE CAMP'S OWN COUNT AND IT DOES NOT
    MATCH THE WIKI'S FOUNDING DATE CLEANLY. 1988 − 93 = 1895. This project dates
    the founding to 1894. The gap is one year and there are ordinary
    explanations — counting completed seasons rather than years, counting from
    the first full season, or a round number chosen by whoever wrote the
    advertisement. IT IS NOT EVIDENCE AGAINST 1894 and is not offered as such.
    What it is worth is that it is the CAMP counting, in public, in its own
    advertising, and history/oldest-camp-question.md is built on exactly this
    kind of self-description.

(c) The camp advertised in Concordia's paper and McGill's in the same seasons,
    which sits with the 1948, 1949 and 1962 advertisements already held: a
    continuous practice of recruiting counsellors out of the city's universities.

===============================================================================
2. VOL. 12 NO. 38, 17 MARCH 1992 — THE SEAMAN FUND'S EVENT HAS A NAME
===============================================================================

  "Friday, March 20. A. ROSS SEAMAN MEMORIAL CUP: friendly competition of
  'SPACEBALL' between LEISURE STUDIES, APSS, DAWSON'S CRLT PROGRAMME, AND YMCA'S
  CAMP KANAWANA. Also: variety show, t-shirts, buffet dinner, an auction, &
  awards. 2:30pm, Loyola Campus Athletic Complex, 7141 Sherbrooke St. W. Info:
  Anita 489-7723."

(Repeated in vol. 12 no. 39.)

WHY THIS MATTERS. wiki/people/a-ross-seaman.md records that the memorial fund
"is notable for raising money through an annual awards evening with auction —
described as possibly the only active Concordia scholarship using this
fundraising model." That is the whole of what this project knew about the event.
Here is the event: it had a NAME, the A. Ross Seaman Memorial Cup; a FORMAT, a
Spaceball tournament; a VENUE, the Loyola Campus Athletic Complex; and — the
part that matters — ITS FOUR TEAMS ARE THE FOUR CONSTITUENCIES NAMED IN THE
SCHOLARSHIP'S OWN TERMS. Concordia's calendar says the award honours Seaman's
dedication "to the communities of Concordia University, Dawson College, Kamp
Kanawana and the YMCA" and that "each year, students from these four
institutions are recognized." Leisure Studies and Applied Social Science are the
two Concordia departments Seaman taught in; CRLT is the Dawson programme he
built; Camp Kanawana is the camp. THE FOUR COMMUNITIES OF THE SCHOLARSHIP PLAYED
A BALL GAME AGAINST EACH OTHER TO RAISE THE MONEY FOR IT.

It also joins up with the 2007 bursary booklet read earlier today, one of whose
citations praises a winner as an "active member in the CRLT Community" who
"worked on the T-shirt Committee, A. Ross Seaman Cup and Bill Lewis Race at the
YMCA" — the t-shirts and the Cup both appear in this notice, and "Bill Lewis
Race" remains unidentified.

===============================================================================
3. VOL. 14 NO. 20, 26 NOVEMBER 1993 — "FOLK RHYTHM AND LIGHT SPIRITS"
    by Sarah Musgrave, and it names the naturalist
===============================================================================

A companion piece to the McGill Daily's review of the same show one day earlier,
25 November 1993, already held here. This one is longer and carries three things
the Daily does not.

  "The music largely represents a selection of Day's compositions since he first
  picked up a guitar TWO YEARS AGO ON A TRIP TO INDONESIA. 'I WAS SUFFERING FROM
  CULTURE SHOCK. I JUST DIDN'T WANT TO COME OUT OF THE HUT. SO I BORROWED A
  GUITAR AND PASSED MY TIME INSIDE WRITING SONGS.' HE TRIED OUT HIS MUSIC ON A
  'CAPTIVE AUDIENCE' AT KANAWANA, a summer camp in the Laurentians, where the
  response was overwhelmingly positive. CONCORDIA DANCE STUDENT ELAINE HOOPER
  MET DAY WHEN THEY WORKED TOGETHER AS NATURALISTS AT CAMP. Hooper has a degree
  in biology and her desire to incorporate her ecological and biological
  knowledge into her performance was in keeping with Day's environmental
  themes."

Also: Day "is presently training for a future in OPERA"; the line-up is "three
vocalists, a couple of guitarists, a trumpet player, and two dancers," aged 17
to 30; songs by Day and McGill student Hartley Wynberg; the other dancer is
Alorani Martin; the show is called "Spirit Rhythms" here against the Daily's
"Spirit Rhythm."

THE POINT FOR THIS WIKI. wiki/people/sean-day.md quotes Day from the Daily — "I
used to work with a naturalist, mostly in Kanawana. We used to do an 'earth
values' program" — and says in terms: "AND THE NATURALIST IS NOT NAMED. Chris
Adam is the obvious candidate… but Day does not say." THE LINK NAMES A FELLOW
NATURALIST: Elaine Hooper, a Concordia dance student with a biology degree, who
"met Day when they worked together as naturalists at camp."

BE CAREFUL WITH THAT, AND THE ARTICLE IS. Hooper is A naturalist Day worked with
at Kanawana, which makes her a far stronger candidate than Chris Adam for the
one in the quotation. It does not make her THAT naturalist: Day says "a
naturalist," singular and unnamed, and the Link says the two of them worked "as
naturalists," which describes both of them holding the role rather than
identifying his collaborator on the "earth values" programme. The candidate
changes; the question does not close.
